newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK ASLAN CIMENTO TO MEET 1997 TARGETS.
newsitem.headline: TURK ASLAN CIMENTO TO MEET 1997 TARGETS.

text.p: Turkey's cement and ready mixed concrete producer Aslan Cimento, largely owned by French Lafarge Group, would meet the $55 million turnover target in 1997, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
"Our H1 results show that we will meet our $55 million total sales target in 1997 against $53 million last year," Benoit Madre, chief executive officer of the company, told Reuters.
Madre said, as Lafarge Turkey they would maintan their 10 percent share in the Turkish cement market.
Shares of the company traded at 90,000 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Wednesday, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
"We expect to sell 1.2 million tonnes of cement this year, equal to last year's amount," Madre said.
"The net average cement price rose to $46 to $46.5 per tonne this year from last year's $45. This will help us to achieve a real increase of three percent in turnover this year," he added.

Aslan Cimento reported 1.3 trillion lira turnover in the first three months of 1997, against 511 billion lira in the same 1996 period. Its three-month loss shrank to 110 billion lira from previous 625 billion.
The company operates a total of 18 ready mixed concrete stations in Turkey's northwestern, Aegean and Mediteranean regions under Lafarge and Lafarge-Ekmel brands.
It aims to sell 1.4 million cubic metres of Lafarge ready mixed concrete this year, against 1.34 million cubic metres in 1996.

The company also operates eight more ready mixed concrete stations under a 50/50 joint venture deal with Yibitas in central Turkey, under Yibitas-Lafarge brand. The venture plans to sell 847,000 cubic meters this year, same as in 1996.
Aslan Cimento spent $15 million for modernisation and a new cement mill last year and plans to spend three million dollars each in 1997 and 1998, to raise the productivity.
Madre said Lafarge Turkey also prepared to break the ground in central Turkey to set up a new cement factory.
Madre who is also the general manager for Lafarge's Mediteranean region, said the new plant would be located 50 km near the capital Ankara.
"The $100 million investment will be a 50/50 joint venture with Yibitas group and we will produce the first package of cement in the year 2001," Madre said.
The new plant will have one million tonnes of annual production capacity.
Madre who estimates a three percent growth for the Turkish cement sector in 1997, expects another three percent growth in next year.
"The Turkish cement market was 32 million tonnes last year and we expect it to rise to 33 million tonnes this year and to around 34 million tonnes next year," he said.

Lafarge Turkey is the major shareholder in Aslan Cimento and cement mill Lafarge Eregli and has a 50 percent share in three cement plants in Yozgat, Sivas, Corum and three mills in Hasanoglan, Nevsehir and Samsun.
